from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the scene layout with title and lecture lines
        title_str = "Prerequisite: The Modulo Sorting Machine"
        lines_str = [
            'Odd numbers sorted by remainder when divided by four.',
            'Group one: remainders of one, called four-k plus one.',
            'Group two: remainders of three, called four-k plus three.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines_str)
        
        # Define colors as specified in animation description
        BOX_COLOR = "#00FF00"   # Modulo 4 Box
        GOLD_COLOR = "#FFD700"  # Gold Bucket
        SILVER_COLOR = "#C0C0C0" # Silver Bucket

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight current lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BOX_COLOR))
        
        # Animation 1: A horizontal row of odd numbers (3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13) enters from the left
        nums = [3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13]
        num_mobs = VGroup(*[Text(str(n), font_size=36) for n in nums])
        
        # Initial positions: Start off-screen left at the vertical level of Row B (y=1.2)
        for i, mob in enumerate(num_mobs):
            mob.move_to(np.array([-4, 1.2, 0]))
            
        self.play(
            AnimationGroup(*[
                mob.animate.move_to(self.grid[f"B{i+1}"])
                for i, mob in enumerate(num_mobs)
            ], lag_ratio=0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Animation 2: A central processing box labeled 'Modulo 4' appears in the middle
        box_rect = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=1.6, color=BOX_COLOR)
        box_label = Text("Modulo 4", font_size=22, color=BOX_COLOR)
        box_group = VGroup(box_rect, box_label)
        self.place_in_area(box_group, "C3", "D4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(box_group))
        
        # Visual transition: Numbers move into the sorting box for "processing"
        box_center = box_group.get_center()
        self.play(
            num_mobs.animate.scale(0.5).move_to(box_center).set_opacity(0.4),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight current lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GOLD_COLOR))
        
        # Animation 3: Two containers appear
        # Gold Bucket (4k+1) positioned in area E1-F3
        gold_rect = Rectangle(width=2.3, height=1.6, color=GOLD_COLOR)
        gold_label = Text("Gold Bucket\n(4k+1)", font_size=16, color=GOLD_COLOR, line_spacing=0.8)
        gold_bucket = VGroup(gold_rect, gold_label)
        self.place_in_area(gold_bucket, "E1", "F3")
        
        # Silver Bucket (4k+3) positioned in area E4-F6
        silver_rect = Rectangle(width=2.3, height=1.6, color=SILVER_COLOR)
        silver_label = Text("Silver Bucket\n(4k+3)", font_size=16, color=SILVER_COLOR, line_spacing=0.8)
        silver_bucket = VGroup(silver_rect, silver_label)
        self.place_in_area(silver_bucket, "E4", "F6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(gold_bucket), FadeIn(silver_bucket))
        
        # Animation 4: The numbers 5, 9, and 13 move from the center and drop into the Gold Bucket
        # Index mapping: 3->0, 5->1, 7->2, 9->3, 11->4, 13->5
        gold_indices = [1, 3, 5]
        gold_targets = VGroup(*[num_mobs[i] for i in gold_indices])
        
        self.play(
            gold_targets.animate.set_opacity(1).scale(1.4).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3).move_to(gold_rect.get_center()),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight current lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SILVER_COLOR))
        
        # Animation 5: The numbers 3, 7, and 11 move from the center and drop into the Silver Bucket
        silver_indices = [0, 2, 4]
        silver_targets = VGroup(*[num_mobs[i] for i in silver_indices])
        
        self.play(
            silver_targets.animate.set_opacity(1).scale(1.4).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3).move_to(silver_rect.get_center()),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_str = "Dirichlet’s Discovery: Infinite Tracks"
        lines_str = [
            'Primes appear in both arithmetic progression tracks infinitely often.',
            'Dirichlet proved primes populate these sequences without end.',
            'No matter how far, prime runners keep appearing.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines_str)

        # Colors
        COLOR_T1 = "#FFD700"  # Gold
        COLOR_T2 = "#C0C0C0"  # Silver
        HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW
        
        # Helper for mapping values to the grid's X range (Col 1 to 6)
        def n_to_x(n, n_max=20):
            # Map [0, n_max] to x in [0.5, 5.5]
            return 0.5 + (n / n_max) * 5.0

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT))
        
        # Animation 1: Two parallel horizontal lines
        track1 = Line(self.grid["B1"], self.grid["B6"], color=COLOR_T1, stroke_width=4)
        track2 = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D6"], color=COLOR_T2, stroke_width=4)
        
        label1 = Text("Track 4k + 1", font_size=20, color=COLOR_T1)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "A1")
        label2 = Text("Track 4k + 3", font_size=20, color=COLOR_T2)
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "C1")

        self.play(Create(track1), Create(track2), Write(label1), Write(label2))
        self.wait(1)

        # Animation 2: Prime numbers 5, 13, 17 on top track
        primes1 = [5, 13, 17]
        dots1 = VGroup(*[
            Dot(point=[n_to_x(p), self.grid["B1"][1], 0], color=COLOR_T1, radius=0.08)
            for p in primes1
        ])
        labels_p1 = VGroup(*[
            Text(str(p), font_size=16, color=COLOR_T1).next_to(dots1[i], UP, buff=0.1)
            for i, p in enumerate(primes1)
        ])

        # Animation 3: Prime numbers 3, 7, 11, 19 on bottom track
        primes2 = [3, 7, 11, 19]
        dots2 = VGroup(*[
            Dot(point=[n_to_x(p), self.grid["D1"][1], 0], color=COLOR_T2, radius=0.08)
            for p in primes2
        ])
        labels_p2 = VGroup(*[
            Text(str(p), font_size=16, color=COLOR_T2).next_to(dots2[i], UP, buff=0.1)
            for i, p in enumerate(primes2)
        ])

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(d) for d in dots1], lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.play(FadeIn(labels_p1))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(d) for d in dots2], lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.play(FadeIn(labels_p2))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        
        # Animation 4: Zoom out simulation
        # Scale current elements down and shift left to represent 0-100 scale
        # We transform the dots to their new positions in the 0-100 range.
        
        new_dots1 = VGroup(*[
            Dot(point=[n_to_x(p, 100), self.grid["B1"][1], 0], color=COLOR_T1, radius=0.04)
            for p in primes1
        ])
        new_dots2 = VGroup(*[
            Dot(point=[n_to_x(p, 100), self.grid["D1"][1], 0], color=COLOR_T2, radius=0.04)
            for p in primes2
        ])
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(labels_p1), FadeOut(labels_p2),
            Transform(dots1, new_dots1),
            Transform(dots2, new_dots2),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Extend lines visually by adding "..." or arrows
        arrow1 = Arrow(self.grid["B6"], self.grid["B6"] + RIGHT * 0.4, color=COLOR_T1, buff=0)
        arrow2 = Arrow(self.grid["D6"], self.grid["D6"] + RIGHT * 0.4, color=COLOR_T2, buff=0)
        self.play(Create(arrow1), Create(arrow2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        
        # Animation 5: More dots pop up rapidly
        # More primes in 4k+1: 29, 37, 41, 53, 61, 73, 89, 97
        # More primes in 4k+3: 23, 31, 43, 47, 59, 67, 71, 79, 83
        extra_primes1 = [29, 37, 41, 53, 61, 73, 89, 97]
        extra_primes2 = [23, 31, 43, 47, 59, 67, 71, 79, 83]
        
        extra_dots1 = VGroup(*[
            Dot(point=[n_to_x(p, 100), self.grid["B1"][1], 0], color=COLOR_T1, radius=0.04)
            for p in extra_primes1
        ])
        extra_dots2 = VGroup(*[
            Dot(point=[n_to_x(p, 100), self.grid["D1"][1], 0], color=COLOR_T2, radius=0.04)
            for p in extra_primes2
        ])
        
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(d) for d in extra_dots1], lag_ratio=0.1),
            LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(d) for d in extra_dots2], lag_ratio=0.1),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset lecture colors
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize basic layout
        lecture_lines = [
            'Despite both being infinite, a subtle race exists.',
            'Team four-k plus three usually leads the prime count.',
            'This preference is known as the famous Chebyshev’s Bias.',
            'Primes favor the silver bucket over the gold bucket.',
            'Even in infinity, numbers exhibit a mysterious rhythmic bias.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Prime Race: Chebyshev’s Bias", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        GOLD_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        SILVER_COLOR = "#C0C0C0"
        CYAN_COLOR = "#00FFFF"

        # Define scoreboard components
        scoreboard_bg = Rectangle(width=5, height=3.5, color=GREY_E, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(scoreboard_bg, "B1", "E6")
        
        label_4k1 = Text("Team 4k+1", color=GOLD_COLOR, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_4k1, "C2")
        
        label_4k3 = Text("Team 4k+3", color=SILVER_COLOR, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_4k3, "C5")

        count_4k1 = Text("0", color=GOLD_COLOR, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(count_4k1, "D2")

        count_4k3 = Text("0", color=SILVER_COLOR, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(count_4k3, "D5")

        bias_title = Text("Chebyshev's Bias", color=CYAN_COLOR, font_size=36)
        self.place_in_area(bias_title, "A2", "A5")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(scoreboard_bg))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SILVER_COLOR)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(label_4k1),
            FadeIn(label_4k3),
            FadeIn(count_4k1),
            FadeIn(count_4k3)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(CYAN_COLOR)
        # Chebyshev's Bias appears in glowing text
        self.play(Write(bias_title))
        self.play(bias_title.animate.set_stroke(CYAN_COLOR, width=2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GOLD_COLOR)
        
        # Simulated fast counting
        # We'll use a sequence of updates to simulate a rapid race
        intermediate_values = [
            ("124,532", "124,541"),
            ("489,201", "489,235"),
            ("812,045", "812,098"),
            ("999,958", "1,000,042")
        ]

        for val1, val3 in intermediate_values:
            new_count1 = Text(val1, color=GOLD_COLOR, font_size=32)
            new_count3 = Text(val3, color=SILVER_COLOR, font_size=32)
            self.place_at_grid(new_count1, "D2")
            self.place_at_grid(new_count3, "D5")
            
            self.play(
                Transform(count_4k1, new_count1),
                Transform(count_4k3, new_count3),
                run_time=0.5
            )

        # Final highlight on the lead
        rect_lead = SurroundingRectangle(count_4k3, color=SILVER_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect_lead))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Subtle "rhythmic" bias effect - a pulse on the silver team
        self.play(
            count_4k3.animate.scale(1.2),
            rect_lead.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialization
        title_text = "The Bridge to Pi: The Leibniz Connection"
        lecture_lines = [
            'These two buckets unexpectedly bridge algebra to geometry.', 
            'Alternating reciprocals of these odd numbers calculate pi.', 
            'Positive terms from gold bucket, negative from silver bucket.', 
            'Summing these fractions reveals a hidden circular pattern.', 
            'The infinite series converges exactly to pi over four.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Constants
        GOLD_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        SILVER_COLOR = "#C0C0C0"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#00BFFF" # DeepSkyBlue
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Leibniz formula building
        formula_parts = VGroup(
            Text("1"),          # 0
            Text("-"),          # 1
            Text("1/3"),        # 2
            Text("+"),          # 3
            Text("1/5"),        # 4
            Text("-"),          # 5
            Text("1/7"),        # 6
            Text("+"),          # 7
            Text("..."),        # 8
            Text("="),          # 9
            Text("π/4")         # 10
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
        
        self.place_in_area(formula_parts, "A1", "B6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.play(FadeIn(formula_parts, shift=UP))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color specific terms based on their source buckets
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GOLD_COLOR)
        
        self.play(
            formula_parts[0].animate.set_color(GOLD_COLOR),  # Denominator 1 (4k+1)
            formula_parts[4].animate.set_color(GOLD_COLOR),  # Denominator 5 (4k+1)
            formula_parts[2].animate.set_color(SILVER_COLOR), # Denominator 3 (4k+3)
            formula_parts[6].animate.set_color(SILVER_COLOR), # Denominator 7 (4k+3)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Geometry: Circle and jagged area approximation
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Define a circle outline
        circle_outline = Circle(radius=0.75, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(circle_outline, "D1", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        center_pos = circle_outline.get_center()
        
        self.play(Create(circle_outline))
        
        # Create visual bars to represent adding/subtracting terms
        bar_gold = Rectangle(height=1.2, width=0.4, color=GOLD_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6)
        bar_silver = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=0.4, color=SILVER_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6)
        bars = VGroup(bar_gold, bar_silver).arrange(RIGHT, aligned_edge=DOWN, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(bars, "D5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Jagged visualization (Star as a proxy for an irregular area)
        jagged_area = Star(n=8, inner_radius=0.4, outer_radius=0.8, color=GOLD_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.4)
        jagged_area.move_to(center_pos)
        
        self.play(
            GrowFromCenter(jagged_area),
            FadeIn(bars, shift=RIGHT)
        )
        
        # Visual "pulse" of adding/subtracting
        self.play(
            jagged_area.animate.scale(0.85).set_color(SILVER_COLOR),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The jagged shape transforms into a smooth circle

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        lines = [
            'Prime distribution directly dictates the value of pi.',
            'Algebraic sorting machines construct the most fundamental constant.',
            'Geometry emerges from the rhythm of prime remainders.',
            'From infinite tracks to the perfect symmetry of circles.',
            'The secret rhythm of primes defines our mathematical universe.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Order from Prime Chaos", lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_1 = YELLOW
        COLOR_2 = GREEN
        COLOR_3 = TEAL
        COLOR_4 = "#FF00FF" # Glowing Pi
        COLOR_5 = ORANGE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_1)
        
        # Representing "Sorting buckets" from Section 1
        bucket_1 = Rectangle(height=0.8, width=0.8, color=COLOR_1)
        bucket_2 = Rectangle(height=0.8, width=0.8, color=COLOR_1)
        self.place_at_grid(bucket_1, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(bucket_2, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Representing "Tracks" from Section 2
        track_1 = Line(start=self.grid["B3"], end=self.grid["B6"], color=COLOR_2)
        track_2 = Line(start=self.grid["E3"], end=self.grid["E6"], color=COLOR_2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(bucket_1), FadeIn(bucket_2),
            Create(track_1), Create(track_2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_2)
        
        # Overlapping/Moving them into a construction area
        construction_area = VGroup(bucket_1, bucket_2, track_1, track_2)
        self.play(
            construction_area.animate.move_to(self.grid["D4"]),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_3)
        
        # Prepare Pi components
        # Top bar
        pi_top = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.2, width=3.0, color=COLOR_4, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_top, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Left leg (with a little hook)
        pi_leg_l = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.5, width=0.2, color=COLOR_4, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_leg_l, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        pi_leg_l.shift(RIGHT * 0.5) # Manual adjustment within grid logic for spacing
        
        # Right leg
        pi_leg_r = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.5, width=0.2, color=COLOR_4, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_leg_r, "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        pi_leg_r.shift(LEFT * 0.5)

        pi_group = VGroup(pi_top, pi_leg_l, pi_leg_r)

        # Morph Animation
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(track_1, pi_top),
            ReplacementTransform(track_2, pi_leg_l),
            ReplacementTransform(bucket_1, pi_leg_r),
            FadeOut(bucket_2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_4)
        
        # Add a glow effect (simple scale pulses)
        self.play(
            pi_group.animate.scale(1.1).set_color(COLOR_4),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            pi_group.animate.scale(1/1.1),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_5)
        
        final_text = Text("The Hidden Rhythm of Primes", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            Write(final_text),
            pi_group.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Secret Rhythm of Primes: From Dirichlet's Theorem to the Geometry of Pi
outline.target_audience: Advanced high school students or undergraduate math enthusiasts

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Modulo Sorting Machine
sections.content: Introduce the concept of modular arithmetic as a 'sorting machine.' Explain that all odd numbers (where primes live, except 2) fall into two buckets when divided by 4: those that leave a remainder of 1 (4k+1) and those that leave a remainder of 3 (4k+3).
sections.example: Visualize a conveyor belt of numbers: 5, 9, 13 drop into the 'Gold Bucket' (4k+1), while 3, 7, 11 drop into the 'Silver Bucket' (4k+3).

sections.title: Dirichlet’s Discovery: Infinite Tracks
sections.content: Introduce Dirichlet's Theorem on Arithmetic Progressions. It states that if the starting number and the step size share no common factors, the sequence contains infinitely many primes. This proves that primes aren't just random; they are distributed across these 'lanes' forever.
sections.example: Imagine two infinite racing tracks. Track A (4k+1) and Track B (4k+3). Dirichlet proves that 'Prime Runners' will appear on both tracks infinitely many times, no matter how far you zoom out.

sections.title: The Prime Race: Chebyshev’s Bias
sections.content: Discuss the 'pattern' within the infinity. While both tracks have infinite primes, Track 4k+3 usually has a slight lead in the count. This subtle imbalance is known as Chebyshev's Bias, showing that primes have a 'preference' in their distribution.
sections.example: A scoreboard showing 'Team 4k+3' with 1,000,042 primes and 'Team 4k+1' with 999,958 primes. A character, 'The Prime Referee,' points out the narrow but persistent lead.

sections.title: The Bridge to Pi: The Leibniz Connection
sections.content: Connect these prime patterns to geometry. Introduce the Gregory-Leibniz series: 1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - 1/7... = π/4. Explain that the denominators are simply the odd numbers from our 4k+1 (positive terms) and 4k+3 (negative terms) buckets.
sections.example: An animation of a circle. Each time a number from the 4k+1 bucket appears, we add a piece to the circle's area; each time a 4k+3 appears, we subtract a smaller piece. Eventually, the jagged edges smooth out into a perfect circle.

sections.title: Synthesis: Order from Prime Chaos
sections.content: Summarize how Dirichlet's algebraic distribution of primes directly informs the calculation of π. Emphasize that the way primes are 'filed' into remainder buckets is what allows us to approximate the most fundamental constant of circles.
sections.example: A final visual montage: The sorting machine from Section 1 zooms out to become the infinite tracks of Section 2, which then bend and curve to form the perimeter of a glowing Pi symbol.

storyboard.title: The Prime Race: Chebyshev’s Bias
lecture_lines: A subtle race exists between these two infinite teams.
The silver team usually maintains a persistent lead.

storyboard.title: The Bridge to Pi: The Leibniz Connection
lecture_lines: These buckets bridge the gap between numbers and geometry.
We alternate fractions from each bucket in a series.
This algebraic pattern begins to construct a circle.
Positive and negative terms balance to find the area.
The infinite sum converges exactly to pi over four.

lecture_lines: Prime distribution directly dictates the value of pi.
